draft.title: Electromagnets
card: An electric current in a wire makes a magnetic field around the wire. Winding the wire into a coil makes this field stronger, and the coil acts like a bar magnet.
This magnet works only while current flows. Switch the current off and the magnetism stops, or almost stops.
An electromagnet is made stronger by adding more turns of wire to the coil, by increasing the current, or by putting an iron core inside the coil.
Electromagnets are useful because they can be switched on and off and their strength can be changed. A scrapyard crane uses one to lift scrap steel and then drop it.
draft.remember: Current in a coil makes a magnet that can be switched off, and more turns, more current or an iron core make it stronger.

a.q: Which change would make an electromagnet weaker?
opts: Lowering the current in the coil
Adding an iron core to the coil
Winding more turns into the coil
Keeping the current switched on for longer
a.why: A smaller current gives a weaker magnetic field, so the electromagnet is weaker. An iron core and more turns both make it stronger, and leaving the current on does not change its strength.
a.clue: Think about what makes the magnetic field in the coil.

b.q: Tom wants a scrapyard crane magnet to drop its load of steel on cue. Which feature of an electromagnet lets him do this?
opts: Its magnetism stops when the current is switched off
Its magnetism gets stronger with a longer wire
Its magnetism lasts after the iron core is removed
Its magnetism changes if the coil is turned around
b.why: An electromagnet works only while current flows, so cutting the current releases the steel. The other options describe things the card does not say: a longer wire alone is not what makes it stronger, and the magnetism does not last when the current stops.
b.clue: What happens to the magnet when the power is cut?

wants.brief: A battery connected to a coil of wire wound around an iron nail. Label the battery, the coil, the iron core and the current direction. Show the nail picking up a few paper clips.
wants.why: It shows how the parts of a simple electromagnet fit together.

a.best: Lowering the current in the coil

b.best: Its magnetism stops when the current is switched off
